‘The Innsmouth Terror’ will be a full-length three-act moving picture of a
glamorous dame kidnapped by a tentacled monstrosity. In Technicolor!
The Innsmouth Terror is a classic 1920s scenario for Call of Cthulhu
7th edition, perfect for those looking for a pick-up-and-play scenario set in
Arkham County. Designed for three to five players, it can be run over one
to two sessions (4-8 hours).
The booklet contains:
•
A scenario designed for all levels of experience;
•
Staging advice for running at conventions;
•
Full colour handouts;
•
Five pre-generated investigators;
•
An additional print-friendly version.
This scenario can be run as a stand alone, or as a sequel to Stage Fright at the
Playhouse by the same author.

INTRODUCTION
Lights, Camera, Action!  It is 1923 and the era of silent film is in
full swing. ‘The Innsmouth Terror’ will be a full-length three-act
moving picture of a glamorous dame kidnapped by a tentacled
monstrosity. In Technicolor!
But when a valuable tiara is loaned to, and then summarily
lost by, the production company, the investigators are sent
to find it. They meet a disenfranchised film crew plagued by
delays, a high-strung starlet desperate to get filming over with,
and a new-fangled camera that keeps breaking. The sense of
simmering boredom and frustration grows as the film crew find
little mirth or distraction in the creaking town of Innsmouth.
Just a sea of stoic, salty, scornful faces wishing these city folks
would leave them in peace.
Can the investigators uncover the truth before the stakes get
raised and the Innsmouth Terror shifts into something more
horrifying than what is captured through the lens of a camera?
“We shall swim out to that brooding reef in the sea and dive down through black abysses to Cyclopean and many-columned
Y’ha-nthlei, and in that lair of the Deep Ones we shall dwell amidst wonder and glory for ever.”
—H.P. Lovecraft, The Shadow over Innsmouth
PREPARING FOR PLAY
The Innsmouth Terror borrows heavily from the story The
Shadow over Innsmouth (1936) by H.P. Lovecraft and utilizes
some of the extended world building from Chaosium’s Escape
from Innsmouth (1992). However, knowledge of these books is
not required to play in, or run this investigation.
This scenario is intended to follow on from the scenario Stage
Fright at the Playhouse, itself a sequel to Edge of Darkness.
However, the scenario stands on its own and can be thought of
as sharing a universe and some NPCs with these other scenarios,
rather than being a direct sequel.
Short on time? The investigation can start in Innsmouth
(Investigation, page 13). You’ll just need to quickly explain
how the investigators got to this point.

The town of Innsmouth is a strange place. New England society
has done its level best to ignore and forget this decrepit seaside
village. Once a thriving port town, these days the harbor is full of
silt, and only local fishing boats come and go with the tide. The
train connection was abandoned not long after it was opened,
the operators calling it the ‘least profitable line’ they had ever
serviced. No one wanted to go to Innsmouth. And no one ever
seemed to leave.
Back in the 1830s, Captain Obed Marsh of Innsmouth made a
deal with the creatures that live below the Devil Reef, a dangerous
set of shallows offshore from the harbor. The creatures supplied
him with golden-alloy trinkets in exchange for glass and rubber
jewelry. Marsh smelted down the trinkets and sold the pure gold,
bringing wealth into the town and making the Marsh family
rich and powerful. Those who benefited from the gold trade
started a church they called the ‘Esoteric Order of Dagon’, a cult
worshiping Dagon, god of the sea. The Esoteric Order slowly
conquered the town of Innsmouth, driving out or converting
everyone. But the embattled authorities fought back, jailing
Obed Marsh and his disciples. The creatures, known as Deep
Ones, then moved in to protect their worshipers, killing local
law enforcement, and cementing Obed Marsh as the unspoken
leader of the town of Innsmouth. This support came at a cost,
and the members of the order were forced to take three oaths:
The First Oath: “Iä! Dagon! I, (speaker’s name), do solemnly
swear that I will neither interfere with, nor inform upon, the
activities of the Deep Ones. Iä! Dagon!”
 The Second Oath: “Iä! Dagon! I, (speaker’s name) do
solemnly swear that, if requested to do so, I will render aid to
the Deep Ones to the best of my ability, and in whatever form
or manner is required of me. Iä! Dagon!”
 The Third Oath: “Iä! Dagon! I, (speaker’s name) do solemnly
swear that I take this entity [a Deep One] as my wife/husband,
that I shall take them to my home, and that with them I will
endeavor to have and raise children, so that the race, and the
faith, can continue to prosper. Iä! Dagon! Iä! Hydra!”
And so, with the third oath, Hybrids were born—offspring
from the union between Deep One and human. Hybrids are
born looking entirely human, but as they reach adulthood and
mature, they begin to take on Deep One traits, such as enlarged
eyes, webbed fingers and other markers of their heritage. This
tends to be called the ‘Innsmouth look’. Eventually, most of the
Hybrids become able to breathe underwater, and they slip into
the sea and join their people down in the depths below.
Ginny Dubois (Born Ginny Brewster, page 4) is one such
child. Precocious and unreasonable, as many children are, Ginny
ran away to study theatre. In doing so, she set a new standard in
outrageously awful acting. Ginny is the prototypical starlet: she
bought her way into various roles using stolen family money,
but eventually even that wasn’t enough to convince Directors to
let her anywhere near a paying audience.
It is now 1923, and Ginny has struck luck once more. She is to
play the leading role in an experimental new film, The Innsmouth
Terror, and it’s going to make her a star! Sure, she has to go back
home for filming, but she’s made a few adjustments to the script
to poke fun at her backwards little village and their backwards
ways.
When a Deep One artifact turned up on set, Ginny was asked
to wear it as part of her costume. Disgusted by the idea, Ginny
stole it and hid it in her old bedroom in Innsmouth.
Ginny doesn’t know that the Director of the film, P.A.
Bazzledon (page 4) is himself in league with Mother Hydra.
He hasn’t hired Ginny for her looks, her money, or her talent.
He has hired her to be sacrificed to a Star Spawn of the god
emperor Cthulhu in front of the citizenry of Innsmouth, to be an
unwitting stooge in a terrifying ritual, and to let all of Innsmouth
know the fate of those that would betray their oaths.

INVOLVING THE INVESTIGATORS
The investigators receive a letter from the Vice Chancellor of
Miskatonic University informing them that the Orne Library,
the main library of the University, loaned out one of its treasured
artifacts to Bazzledon Productions for use in an experimental
film. However, while onsite in the seaside town of Innsmouth,
the production company has lost the artifact and suspects theft.
The investigators have been tasked with recovering the jewelry
and bringing back any evidence of the culprit so that it can be
handed over to the local constabulary (Handout 1-a: letter).
The Innsmouth Terror assumes that the investigators are
members of the Society for the Exploration of the Unexplained
(SEU) and are students or employees of the Miskatonic
University. However, they could equally be professionals or
another group hired to work for the University; the Keeper
simply needs to use Handout 1-b (letter).
THE INNSMOUTH TERROR
Technology is changing rapidly! Moving pictures are the latest
big thing and there is a rush to develop color in film. While postproduction coloring has been around for a while, the dream has
always been to capture color in real time. In 1923, technicolor
refers to a prism beam-splitting system, where two black and
white films are recorded simultaneously, one behind a red filter,
and another behind a green filter. The process is complex, prone
to slipping out of alignment and, at best, finicky. Production
constantly must stop while the engineer fixes and tinkers with
the single camera capable of this feat.
The working title of this movie is The Innsmouth Terror. In
the story, a young girl (played by Ginny Dubois) is fleeing from
an abusive family. She then finds herself captured by evil froglike creatures whilst running dramatically across a field. The
frog-like men trap her inside a cave and taunt her. They then
attempt to feed her to a giant tentacled monster. Luckily, the
girl is saved at the last minute by an ingenious young man in a
bowler hat, who throws a packet of Tum-Eez, an antacid, down
the monster’s throat.
Many of the finer details of the movie, such as the appearance of
the frog-like men, have been adapted by Ginny to be particularly
offensive towards Innsmouth locals, who have noticed that the
cheaply-made costumes of the frog-men bear a not-so-striking
resemblance to the Deep Ones.
During the scenario, production moves chronologically
through the movie:
•
When the investigators arrive, filming is taking place
across a dramatic field beside the train tracks, just outside
of Innsmouth.
•
During the investigation, filming moves into the caves of
Innsmouth, where the prison scene is being shot.
•
In the finale, filming has moved to a cliff directly above
Innsmouth, where the Star Spawn is summoned in full
view of the citizenry.
Keeper note:  The Innsmouth Terror isn’t going to be a
‘Talkie’. It’s a silent film. The drive for color and sound in
film all happened around the same time, but both at once?
Madness.
Keeper note: the Society for the Exploration of the
Unexplained (SEU) is informal society made up of students
and professors of the Miskatonic University. This society
is established in the Call of Cthulhu Starter Set. Each time
the SEU finds an interesting avenue of exploration, they
choose the members that seem most capable of tackling the
mystery. The SEU meets once a month in a private reading
room of the Orne Library.

DRAMATIS PERSONAE
Genevieve ‘Ginny’ Dubois, age 25, starlet
In bad light, one might mistake Ginny’s too-wide eyes and
stretched-out smile for innocent beauty. But once the lights are
shining and the cameras are rolling, only the thick makeup and
dramatic angles can hide her slow transformation into a hybrid.
She is determined to ‘hit it big’ before her transformation takes
hold and will go to any lengths to make it so. Born in Innsmouth
to a loving mother and a terrifying, Deep One father in 1897.
It was assumed that one day, Ginny would join her brothers
and sisters down below. However, Ginny had other plans. After
running off with the family gold to study Theatre, she bought
her way into various productions at the Miskatonic Playhouse.
Sponsoring the productions in exchange for the leading role.
However, the shows all bombed. She has now attached herself
to the lead role of The Innsmouth Terror.
Ginny has milky-white skin, and wears far too much makeup.
Her bleached blonde hair is up in curls; her bright red dress is the
same colour as her lipstick and she smells faintly of lavender. A
closer look notes that slightly wide-set eyes, the slightly cracked
skin and the slightly oversized teeth.
P.A. Bazzledon, age 40, director & conman
Phineas Arthur Bazzledon is an up-and-coming director straight
out of New York. Or at least, that’s who he claims to be. With a
tailored suit, a shiny top hat, and an amaranthine waist coat, he
stands out in the crowd. A white man, sporting an impeccably
groomed mustache that sits atop a strong, square jaw so often
associated with power and leadership. The light touch of gray
appearing in his hair only adds to his effortless sophistication.
He rolled into Arkham a few weeks ago and started throwing
money around the local acting scene like it was water. It wasn’t
long before he had the entire dramatic scene circling around
him in a death spiral of devotion. When he announced his plans
to shoot a silent movie in color, he had his pick of local talent.
Bazzledon is not who he appears to be. A con artist, in his
youth, he joined a cult worshiping Dagon, thinking to make a
quick buck. But he found that his oaths to Dagon were not easily
broken. At night his dreams are wracked by Mother Hydra, the
leader of the Deep Ones. She has instructed him to return the
child, Ginny Brewster to Innsmouth and to sacrifice her above
the town. The line of credit he is using to fund this shooting is
entirely phony and it is only a matter of time before he is hunted
down by one of the many loan sharks he has leaned on to funnel
money into this moving picture. But by then, he plans to be well
on his way to his next town, his next mark, and his next con.
Genevieve ‘Ginny’ Dubois

Dramatis Personae
Christopher McGuire, age 37, engineer
A tall, gangly looking white man with curly ginger hair tucked
under a flat cap, Christoper McGuire is an awkward soul who
only seems to come to life when he is working with technology.
Incredibly tall and perennially hunched over his camera, he owns
a small workshop just outside the grounds of the Miskatonic
University. He has been known to give the occasional guest
lecture to the Engineering department, though less frequently
these days, as none of the academics are quite sure what he’s
up to.
It was McGuire that pitched the idea of filming in technicolor
to Bazzledon not long after he arrived in Arkham. And Bazzledon
seized on the idea as the perfect long con.
Sadly, the technology really isn’t ready for a full-length film.
It isn’t really ready to be taken out of the lab. The camera keeps
breaking, prompting multi-hour pauses during filming where
production grinds to a halt. McGuire is doing everything he can
to keep the process going.
McGuire is desperate to make the film work and has invested
all his savings into this endeavor. He needs the film to be
completed and will keep the camera rolling to the very end.
Anna Díaz, age 26, producer
A technically brilliant, funny, well read, hard-working actress,
Anna long ago gave up on her chances of ever making it big. The
starring roles go to elegant, blond-haired bombshells, not solidlooking farm girls with dark brown skin and acne scars.
However, her near encyclopedic knowledge of the Arkham
scene and her ability to sort out just about anything made her
the perfect hire for producer of The Innsmouth Terror. Not that
Anna has ever produced a film before, but she’s done plenty of
stage shows and it can’t be that different, right?
It was Anna who sourced the old train cart that the crew are
living in. She got it at a steal, and it’s far comfier than the tents
that the crew would normally sleep in when on-site. It’s also
been a complete life saver now that production is dragging on
day after day, as there are no decent hotels in Innsmouth.
Working with a ‘cinematic genius’ like Bazzledon has been
difficult for Anna. His demands are often unexpected and unlike
anything Anna would ever imagine. However, she is just happy
to be learning from someone with so much experience. And
mostly she’s learning on the job, figuring things out herself.
Even if that’s not exactly what she expected to be learning.
Anna didn’t get to where she was by not seizing every
opportunity presented to her, so she’s going to make this
production a success, if she has to drag it kicking and screaming
across the line.
Anna Díaz
Christopher McGuire

Dramatis Personae
MINOR NPCs
Diane Loring
The diligent head of research at the Orne Library. She helps the
investigators in their search through the archives and point them
towards the Arkham Advertiser. She is a serious, dark-skinned
woman in her late 40s with naturally graying hair. Diane Loring
is courteous to the investigators, though stops short of being
friendly. If any investigators are students, they’ll be aware of
Loring’s fierce reputation. She is always willing to help students
with serious questions, but she dislikes noise or complications
in the library.
Henry Armitage
The famous Head Librarian of the Orne Library may already
be known to the investigators. He may choose to help the
investigators in place of Diane Loring.
Karen Jeffries
The slightly tetchy, opinionated, bossy head of the Arkham
Advertiser, Karen is a firm believer that people never show her
enough respect and will absolutely not have time for a group
of investigators who think their investigation is more important
than the news. However, if they sweet talk her or seem useful,
she will fall over herself to help them out.
Franc Turner
Janitor of the late Miskatonic Playhouse. Franc is a slightly
graying Black man wearing blue overalls and sporting an
impressive mustache. He is tall and broad shouldered and
barely fits into his shirt.
Jeremiah Brewster
Second highest ranking priest in the Esoteric Order of Dagon.
He keeps the residents of the town firmly under control so as not
to upset the Deep Ones. His transformation into a Deep One is
almost complete.
Pete
Proprietor of the Innsmouth General Store. He is cheery
and friendly to the investigators. He clearly doesn’t get much
business and is glad to see some new faces.
Zadok Allen
The infamous drunk from Shadow over Innsmouth. He knows
the full story of Obed Marsh, his deal with the Deep Ones and
the three oaths the people of Innsmouth were forced to swear.
Sammy Brewster, age 21, dilettante & sibling
A perfectly pleasant young white man from a rich family, Sammy
is just starting to show the infamous Innsmouth look: his too
large eyes and slightly fishy features make him more boyish than
handsome; his slick blond hair gives off the impression of being
slightly… damp.
Sammy has been hanging around the production camp trying
to speak to his sister, Ginny. A couple of days ago, he was caught
by the crew, who gave him the black eye he’s now sporting on
his right eye. Ginny has made no move to contact him. She’s just
not interested.
The Crew
An unruly mob of heavyset men and women that do the lifting,
the organizing, and occasionally play secondary roles in the film
such as ‘Scary fish-man number 2’. They can mostly be found
hanging around the production train or doing a variety of jobs
around the set. Infinitely interchangeable and of indeterminate
number, the Crew enjoy getting drunk and hanging around a fire
pit in the evening. A simmering tension exists between the Crew
and the residents of Innsmouth, and more than one fight has
broken out between the groups.
Sammy Brewster

ORNE LIBRARY (MISKATONIC UNIVERSITY)
Our mystery opens in the quiet surroundings of the Orne Library
in the Miskatonic University. The Society for the Exploration
of the Unexplained (SEU) normally only meets once a month
in a private reading room, but this unscheduled meeting has
been quickly pulled together due to a request coming in from
the Vice Chancellor of Miskatonic University themselves! The
Vice Chancellor requires their help in recovering the Atlantean
Jewel, a bizarre looking tiara made of alloyed gold (Handout
1-a: letter). It is the only one of its kind and an archaeological
treasure. The note from the Board says little, other than to
encourage the investigators to contact Diane Loring for
further information.
As events transpired, Henry Armitage, the Head Librarian,
simply unlocked the glass case and handed the artifact over
to P.A. Bazzledon after he provided a signed note from the
Vice Chancellor of the University stating that he had been given
permission to take the item. The note was, of course, a forgery.
An internal review will eventually find Armitage was tricked
into providing the artifact and dock him one week’s wages.
Investigators may be tempted to try and find out who was
responsible for lending out the Jewel to Bazzledon. If they do so,
they find the university staff incredibly uncooperative. Armitage
is well-loved and his employees fiercely protective.
The investigators’ first port of call is most likely to be Diane
Loring, the diligent Head of Research, who works at the main
desk.
Loring explains that the Atlantean Jewel is a treasure that
was housed securely in the Orne Library behind a thickened
glass case. Its exact history and precise origin are the subject
of some fevered debate in certain archaeological circles. Most
scholars believe that it was forged by an ancient, now lost,
civilization, hence the rather uninspiring, name for the artifact.
It was ‘erroneously’ lent out to a production company for the
filming of an experimental film. The production appears to be in
Innsmouth, a small town northeast of Ipswich. No major roads
go to the town, and the only rail connection was through Rowley
closed a few years ago. She believes there is a bus service to
Innsmouth that leaves at 9pm from Dyer Street.
•
Investigators asking how the artifact came to be let
out get a dismissive glare from Loring. She explains
that she believes phony credentials were provided to
an ‘important’ member of the library, who handed the
artifact over in good faith.
•
If asked how the university found out about the theft,
Loring responds that the producer Anna Díaz reported
the loss of the Jewel to the University.
Diane Loring
Dr. Henry Armitage
Keeper note: it is very common for Investigators to come
up with elaborate theories and ask questions that are not
contained within the bounds of the scenario. If they do ask
a question to which there exists no obvious answer, feel
free to improvise an answer that ideally leads them back to
information relevant to the scenario.

THE ARKHAM ADVERTISER
While the Orne Library may be the ideal place for delving into
the past, nowhere can quite beat the upbeat Arkham Advertiser
for the latest news and gossip around town. Its proprietor,
Karen Jeffries, is perhaps, the most self-important gossip
in town. If the investigators arrive during the day, there is a
flurry of activity in the new room as Jeffries and her employees
sit around one large desk, talking excitedly on their phones,
chain smoking cigarettes, passing notes between each other, all
while intermittently typing away at their typewriters. The place
is vibrant and bustling. Investigators attempting to interrupt
Jeffries before she is ready to speak to them get an earful and are
told to wait to the side, where a set of incredibly uncomfortable
green chairs sit. However, if they wait patiently, Jeffries turns
her attention to them after what seems like forever.
•
On a successful Archaeology roll, investigators pull a
little more information from Loring about the artifact. It
is a tiara of an unusual gold alloy, one that modern science
is unable to replicate. Such treasures are occasionally
pulled up from the sea floor by fishermen, who then go
on to sell them. This one is vaguely associated with the
town of Innsmouth, which is why it was likely taken.
•
Loring is not aware of any of the details of the film or
its crew and recommends that investigators contact
the local paper The Arkham Advertiser (adjacent)
to find out more. She further mentions that, of course,
the resources of the Orne Library are available to them
should they need it.
Investigators may take many different avenues of research
when using the Orne Library. To uncover general information
about Innsmouth and the artifact, they can use a general
Library Use roll. They may also use different avenues of
research to come to some general conclusions about the theft:
On a successful Occult roll, investigators are aware that such
artifacts are often highly prized by cults and secret organizations,
who often revere items from lost cultures.
On a successful Anthropology roll, investigators intuit that
the most likely people to steal a cultural treasure are those that it
originally belonged to. They have this rather unusual belief that
the treasure somehow belongs to them.
On a successful Law roll, investigators think it’s probably
best to just follow the money. Who are Bazzledon Productions?
And would they benefit from selling the item?
For more up-to-date information, they would need to talk to
people or visit The Arkham Advertiser (adjacent).
Keeper note: the description of the Jewel will be familiar
to any player who has read The Shadow Over Innsmouth,
and the Keeper can be relatively open with the players
that the tiara is clearly linked to Innsmouth. The Jewel
was made by the Deep Ones and traded to the people of
Innsmouth as part of their ongoing deal. Tiaras like the
Atlantean Jewel are often worn by priests of the Order of
Dagon or melted down to produce gold.
Keeper note: if the investigators have met Karen before,
then she may react differently to them. Karen is best
approached with offers of large sums of money to support
the work of the Arkham Advertiser. Failing that, she is
quite shallow and likes those with high Credit Rating or
Appearance scores.
Karen Jeffries

THE MISKATONIC PLAYHOUSE
Investigators may have connected Ginny Dubois to the
Playhouse and go there searching for clues. Sadly, the Miskatonic
Playhouse has burned down. As the investigators stand outside
the wreckage of this once proud building, the only person visible
is an older Black man, who appears to be cleaning in amongst
the wreckage. This is Franc Turner, the handyman of the
Playhouse.
Franc remembers Ginny Dubois as the starlet of the show. He
describes her as ‘trouble’ and he’s glad to be rid of her. Ginny
seemed to have one aim in mind, and that was to get herself
to Hollywood and become a star. She didn’t seem to care about
who got in her way or why. If investigators pass a Social roll
with Franc, he admits that he heard rumors that all her money
came from her family, and that they’d sent some lawyer after her
attempting to get it back.
Investigators asking Karen for help get nothing for nothing,
and Karen must be convinced with a successful Charm or
Persuade roll, unless they bring her an exclusive story about
how the Orne Library lost a priceless artifact. That interests her
and she is then willing to share what she knows about the various
players if the investigators are willing to provide an anonymous
quote that would bring the great Miskatonic University into
disrepute.
Once Karen does open up though, she is absolutely brimming
with gossip about The Innsmouth Terror.
•
The Director, P.A Bazzledon, appeared in Arkham about
three weeks ago. He came up from New York, where his
name is associated with a number of off-Broadway hits.
It seems he’s a bit of a rising star.
•
Bazzledon has been absolutely throwing money around.
Jeffries would love to know how he made his fortune;
she’s written multiple articles about the mysterious
sources of this theatrical dilettante and rumors abound.
Everything from family money, to piracy, to striking
gold in the west has been suggested. However, the man
remains an enigma.
•
The project is apparently to be filmed in ‘Technicolor’.
The claim is that this produces real color! Jeffries
published a piece about the inventor Christopher
McGuire recently. He’s an oddball that occasionally
works with the University.
•
The star of the film is one Ginny Dubois, who recently
had a run of shows at The Miskatonic Playhouse
(adjacent), before it burned down in mysterious
circumstances. Her acting skills are ‘limited’ but Jeffries
has taken a shine to her. (On a successful Psychology
roll, investigators realize that Ginny donated money to
the Advertiser in exchange for positive reviews. Actually,
it’s pretty obvious on a failed roll, too.)
•
The producer purchased an old rail sleeper train and
had it driven out onto the abandoned rail line from
Innsmouth to Rowley. The whole crew are staying there
as the town of Innsmouth apparently lacks hotels of
sufficient quality.
If asked about Innsmouth, Jeffries makes a face. Apparently,
nothing of importance has happened in Innsmouth in a hundred
years. The only paper, the Innsmouth Courier, went out of
business back in the 1840s. She considers it almost beneath her
to even discuss it. Though, and her voice drops into a whisper,
rumors have it that the starlet Ginny Dubois is, in fact, originally
from Innsmouth. Though she claims she’s from Newburyport.
Keeper note: if the Miskatonic Playhouse did not burn

It is getting late when the investigators arrive in town. As the
bus rolls in, a distinctive fishy odor overwhelms their senses.
The smell is unpleasant and ubiquitous in the center of town,
getting worse as they slowly approach the harbour. It mixes in
with the seaside breeze that is constantly blowing through the
town. The streetlights aren’t on and the night is only lit by the
orange-lamp headlights of the bus. The thundering sound of
multiple waterfalls is audible throughout the town, masking
the queer sounds that emanate from many of the dark, ruined
houses.
The investigators could not telephone ahead to book rooms in
a hotel, as Innsmouth does not have a phone line. The bus driver
croaks quietly to them that there are always rooms available
nearby in The Gilman House Hotel (page 12), and he points
at a building just off the square. Light falls out into the street
from a downstairs window, and the front doors are open. If one
were to squint slightly, it would almost appear inviting.
Investigators can stay at the Gilman House Hotel, or they spot
a firelight at the edge of town. This is the Production Train
Car (page 12), where Anna Díaz will find beds for them.
ARRIVAL
The investigators can take the 9pm coach to Innsmouth from
Dyer Street. It costs 40c and takes a little over 45 minutes. The
coach itself is rickety and travels slowly, however, it drops them
off in New Town Square, Innsmouth. Investigators with a car
may instead choose to travel there in style. However, the road to
Innsmouth is small, bumpy, and badly maintained. The driver
should pass a Drive Auto roll or find they were driving too fast,
blowing out the rear axle on the way to Innsmouth. They are
then forced to hitch a ride with the bus anyway.
Keeper note: it is better that the investigators don’t have
a car as this will limit their ability to remove themselves
from the situation in the town.

THE PRODUCTION TRAIN CAR
On the edge of Innsmouth, to the north-west, a firelight glows.
It is the only point of light visible from sleepy Innsmouth in the
dark—most of the windows are covered up by thick curtains to
keep the light (and sound) in. Investigators following the light
can quickly pick up the abandoned train track and follow it to
the Production Train Car.
Investigators may arrive at the Production Train late in the
evening or early the next morning after spending a disturbing
sleepless night in the Gilman House Hotel.
If they arrive in the evening, then they find various crew
members sitting around a fire sharing stories, drinks, and
laughing together. One of the crew, a well-built woman, stands
up to greet them. This is Anna Díaz, the producer. She introduces
herself but quickly packs them off to one of the sleeper cars to
get some rest, promising to answer all questions in the morning.
They are accommodated in a small, but surprisingly comfortable
room in the train car, with enough beds for the entire group.
They fall asleep to the sounds of laughter and merriment on the
edge of their hearing.
THE GILMAN HOUSE HOTEL
The Gilman House is the infamous hotel from The Shadow over
Innsmouth by H.P. Lovecraft. Some groups may beeline straight
there, anticipating the horror, while others will do their utmost
to avoid it.
Regardless, this once upmarket hotel was built in the 1830s
and is now showing its age. Creaking floorboards and dusty
carpets greet the investigators; flickering gas lights illuminate
the reception. Behind the desk, a pleasant, avuncular looking
receptionist takes their names and assigns them the ‘freshest’
rooms on the top floor. He comments in a smiling way that
they generally use the top floors for ‘out of towners,’ as they
are quieter and the ‘odor’ is ‘less overt’. He knows it takes some
getting used to.
The hotel lacks any semblance of a concierge service and the
receptionist’s advanced age tells the investigators that they will
have to carry their own luggage up the creaking wooden steps
to the top floor in the darkness. The receptionist hands them a
spare lantern if they think to ask for it. He informs them there
will be a lantern in each room and a ‘bedpan’ under each bed.
(The actual toilets are at the far end of the hallway).
As the investigators wander up the stairs, they should all make
Listen rolls. Successful rolls alert the investigators to an array
of odd wheezes, croaks, gasps, and one stifled scream coming
from the lower floors of the hotel. This prompts a Sanity roll
(0/1 loss) from whomever hears the noises.
When they enter their rooms, they find a no-nonsense,
though slightly dated, hotel room. A pail of fresh water sits by
the window, there’s a small writing desk, and a single bed. The
investigators’ rooms are not beside each other, spread out across
the building. The bolt locks on their rooms are flimsy, almost
pointless.
On a successful Spot Hidden roll, investigators notice that
each of their rooms has a connecting door to the one beside it So
two rooms (or more) could be connected to create a small suite.
A more paranoid investigator may realize that someone could
easily enter their room even if they have their door bolted and
barred.
It is at this point that many investigators may choose to
flee the Gilman House Hotel. Nothing bars their way as they
make their apologies and leave. If they do stay the night, the
investigator with the lowest Luck wakes around 3am to the
sound of someone attempting to open their door. If they took no
precautions and didn’t bar the door, instead they hear the door
softly closing, as if someone has been watching them sleep.

Díaz doesn’t want to prejudice the investigators’ inquiries and
wants them to consider all options. That being said, there are
only three places she has been unable to search:
•
P.A Bazzledon’s office: “But why would he steal the
Jewel, he is furious that it’s missing, and he’s the one that
went to such trouble to get it for filming anyway.”
•
Ginny Dubois’ trailer: “But she literally comes from
money. I can’t think of one single reason why she’d
engage in petty theft.”
•
Christopher McGuire’s lab: “He absolutely forbids
anyone from entering there. And for good reason. That’s
where all the delicate technology is stored.”
Her only other lead is that there has been a young man from
Innsmouth hanging around the set. Most of the locals have
been staying well clear of the production, but this one has been
spotted amongst the train cars more than once. Some members
of the crew ran him off a few nights ago. Díaz suspects he is their
strongest lead.
The investigators are also, of course, free to speak to everyone
on the crew. This morning they are doing some ‘re-shoots’ out
on the field beside the train tracks, so everyone will be in one
place.
Díaz is overtly helpful, detail oriented, and entirely honest
with the investigators. She will do anything, within reason, in
her power to help the investigation. With a successful Social
roll, investigators can even convince her to ‘accidentally’ leave
the spare keys for the various train cars on the desk when she
heads out. Otherwise, investigators can attempt to snatch them
with a Sleight of Hand roll, or sneak back into the office and
take them with a successful Stealth roll.
THE PRODUCER’S OFFICE
It is early morning; though the sun is attempting to pierce its way
through, it will be hours before it can burn off the mist blanketing
the Manuxet valley. Anna Díaz sits at her crowded desk, retrofitted into a sleeping compartment of the Production Train. The
smell of fresh coffee fills the room, the window is open, and
birdsong can be heard in the distance. The investigators crowd
into the remaining space of the room. There’s not enough room
for them all to sit, and only one other chair.
Díaz thanks the investigators for coming and apologizes again
for losing the Atlantean Jewel. She understands that it is a
treasure of utmost value and notes how incredibly thankful the
production was that the University agreed to share it with them
in the first place.
As soon as she realized that the Jewel was missing, she notified
the University and conducted a thorough search. In retrospect,
she is embarrassed to admit that she immediately suspected the
Crew. Which isn’t very class conscious of her. She had the Crew
search through each other’s personal effects and paired them up
to look through the entire train. It’s not like the Jewel is small.
So she is fairly certain that it is not hidden on the carriage.
Díaz is unsure of where the Jewel was taken from and no-one
seems to know where it was being stored. Bazzledon believed it
was in McGuire’s Lab. McGuire thought it was stored in a safe
in Bazzledon’s office.

•
Investigators trying to get into the mind of Bazzledon
may use a Psychology or Psychoanalysis while
looking around his room. On a success, they see the
disrepair and disorganization in his private affairs,
and compare it to the detail and care he takes in his
appearance and his make-up. They note that this is a
man who cares about how he is perceived, caring for his
makeup supplies with the same care as one would see
from an artisan caring for his tools.
•
Investigators interested in the makeup may attempt
a Disguise roll to realize that these are the tools of
someone familiar with changing their appearance
regularly, and not just those of a showman who likes to
look good.
Eventually, the investigators notice the locked floor safe
hidden under a creaky floorboard. Breaking in requires a
successful Lockpick roll. They could also unscrew it with a
successful Mechanical Repair roll. Inside, the investigators
uncover $4000 in cash, as well as an old Derringer handgun.
But no tiara.
Investigators can conduct a thorough search of Bazzledon’s
office and come away with no evidence that he has taken the

AROUND THE TRAIN
Set beside the sleeper car, attached to the antiquated steam
engine, a diner car has been hastily converted into a number
of large spaces. Entering from the steam engine side leads to
Bazzledon’s Office (below), the center leads into Ginny’s
Trailer (page 15), and the far side has a small ramp built into

investigators have access to one, the walls are cardboard thin
and can be peeled back, allowing them to move between trailers.
Bazzledon’s Office
The curtains are lazily pulled in this office, letting sharp beams
of light cut through the dim, dusty haze. For the most part,
Bazzledon is never in his office; instead he is always on set,
shouting directions, making plans, and working to bring about
the final scene, the culmination of his plans.
In one corner, a tangled mess of bedsheets indicates the
location of a bed. Beside it, a large trunk full of clothes and a large
mirror takes pride of place. A cold iron rests beside it. In front
of the mirror, a half dozen vials of make-up, gels, and ointments
are neatly stacked. His desk is built out of an old train table and
it is covered in papers. The other side of the room contains two
comfortable looking armchairs, between them sits a small table
with a number of expensive looking liquor bottles on top.
Investigators can take many different avenues of investigation
while in this room, uncovering different information:
The papers on the desk are rather overwhelming and nothing
of value comes out on a quick glance through the dense sheets of

that Bazzledon’s numbers don’t add up. There’s no
attempt to budget or forecast costs for the film. Whatever
reason he has for making this movie, it’s not about cash.

 A Spot Hidden roll uncovers a letter scrunched up and
tossed in the bin. It is from someone named ‘Fat Tony’

money doesn’t make its way back into Tony’s hands

Investigators looking into the scripts can use a
Language (English) or Library Use roll to sift
through the various drafts abandoned in a pile. It
becomes clear that earlier drafts of the script called for

than frog-men. The frog-like additions appear to have

•
Anyone reading the correspondence discovers there was
a bidding war by various companies to sponsor the film.

McGuire’s Lab

On Set
During the initial investigation, everyone involved in the
production is working in a large open field beside the abandoned
rail tracks. The weather today is dramatic, with stormy clouds
threatening thunderstorms later, but for now there’s only a light
breeze blowing.
This is likely the first opportunity the investigators have had
to look over the dramatic landscape of Innsmouth. The valley
below looks to be one extended swamp, but rising up above the
far side of the town, jagged peaks and cliff faces give a feeling
of enclosure and isolation. It’s hard to imagine that this lost bit
of coastline is only a 45 minute bus ride from Arkham. Truly,
modern technology is a marvel.
P.A Bazzledon and Christopher McGuire are quietly arguing
over some technical points by the camera. Meanwhile, Ginny
Dubois is resting on a foldable chair under a giant mink fur coat
in a thick pair of sunglasses, while smoking from a cigarette
holder. Two larger members of the Crew are sitting on the
ground nearby, playing the dice game Twenty-Six. They are
half-dressed as ‘frog-creatures’: their legs are made up to look
scaly and wrong. Lying on the ground beside the Crew, there
is a sort of plastic mold that looks like it covers a person’s
torso, arms, and head, turning them into a plastic-y frog-like
creature. At first glance, it’s a terrifying twisting of plastic lying
haphazardly abandoned on the ground. It is only after the Crew
get up and begin preparing for the scene that investigators truly
comprehend it as a piece of costume.
Keeper note: while to a modern eye, the plastic costumes
may remind them of out-of-date B-movies or Doctor Who
reruns, to the public of the 1920s, elaborate costumes
are quite new and unusual, and the investigators may
genuinely be a little disturbed by it.
Keeper note: have the investigators met Ginny before
whilst playing through Stage Fright? Don’t worry about it.
She doesn’t remember them at all and treats them exactly
the same.

The Railway Entrance
A set of foreboding looking sharp rocks fall against one
another creating a natural arch. Stepping through, a small
grassy area with a lightly trodden path leads towards a
slotted hole that runs down into some naturally forming
tunnels. If investigators saw the glint of light while On Set
(page 17), their eyes dart towards the broken binoculars
lying on a rock. Otherwise, it requires a Spot Hidden to
notice the binoculars.
If investigators have found Handout 2, they can
follow the map instructions from here through The Cave
System (below). It leads to The Brewster Residence
(page 20). If they have no instructions and choose to
enter the caves anyway, they exit the caves through an
abandoned house in central Innsmouth.
THE CAVE SYSTEM
Sitting underneath the town of Innsmouth and its
accompanying cliffs, are a warrenous set of tunnels that
have been used by smugglers and deep ones alike to move
around unseen for generations. Moving through the caves
is awkward. There are no directions, just large, jagged
rocks that have been occasionally cleared to create rough
pathways through the stony labyrinth. Minor additions,
such as cut handholds and the occasional ladder suggest
routes, but frequent cave-ins mean that not all pathways
are trustworthy, or lead somewhere.
Investigators with an idea of where they are heading may
make a Navigate roll in order to try and head that way
through the caves. On a success, they arrive where they
meant to. On a failure, they come up in the entirely wrong
place (normally an abandoned home in Innsmouth).
Throughout the scenario, investigators may return to
the cave system many times. The caves can lead to The
Brewster Residence (page 20), Stumbling onto Set
(Page 21), Into Innsmouth (page 22), and The Esoteric
Order of Dagon (page 24).
Keepers should make sure they are aware of the light
source investigators are using (they likely have a lantern
with them), who is holding the light, and in what order
they are moving through the cave system.
Moving Through the Caves
Whenever the investigators are moving around the
cave, have them roll 1d100 and use Table 2 (page 19) to
generate an encounter. Roll at least two encounters each
time they traverse the caves. If investigators roll the same
result twice, take the entry below the one they rolled.
The standard way for the investigators to move into
the cave system is by finding the entrance by the railway
tracks.
However, there are many entrances to the caves, and
the Keeper should be aware that finding an entrance to the
cave system is an excellent way to move the action along if
the investigation goes off in an unusual direction. In this
case, they can emerge into Stumbling onto Set (page
21).

Residence either before or after talking to Sammy, they find a
dilapidated house, with only a few rooms in use. Most of the rest
of the house is covered in dust. Investigators that get too nosy
risk waking a Shoggoth living in the basement (page 31), and are
forced to run for their lives.
If the investigators look around the ground floor, they step
into a pink frilly room with expensive-looking red furniture
and a comfortable looking bed in one corner. The wardrobe lies
open and clothes cover the small sofa and bed as if someone has
recently rummaged through all the clothes. This is Ginny’s old
room. Hidden underneath the bed, investigators discover the
Atlantean Jewel.
Held up close, the Jewel is intense to look at. A weird, noncongruent pattern of intertwining golden lines forming up the
shape of a tall tiara. A lightly-colored gem sits at the very-top.
It does not look like something a human would make, though it
vaguely reminds investigators of the sea.
If the investigators find the Jewel while Sammy is present, he
gets very worried, telling the investigators that item ‘probably
belongs to Dad’. He gets very excited before attempting to
snatch it and run off with it. The investigator holding it must
succeed on a Hard DEX roll in order to stop him. Sammy then
runs off into the caves, prompting a chase scene that can lead to
The Epic Finale (page 25).
Otherwise, the investigators may re-enter the caves, and
experience the Stumbling onto Set scene (page 21), or if they
have already experienced that scene, then the storm reaches its
apex and they get turned around, exiting in the center of town to
experience The Epic Finale (page 25).
THE BREWSTER RESIDENCE
Investigators can arrive at the Brewster Residence by emerging
from the cave system. If they do, the exit is inside a mundane
gardening shed in the front garden. Alternatively, they may find
the address after speaking to Zadok Allen (The Fire Station,
page 23).
In front of them stands a slightly dilapidated, though clearly
still occupied, three-story house. Around the outside, the
garden is overgrown and untended. On a successful Track roll
investigators pick up a lightly worn track leading from the garden
shed to a back window that doesn’t seem to shut properly. This
window leads into Ginny’s old room.
Knocking on the front door, a young man answers. He has
that fishy, Innsmouth look that so many of the residents have,
though they are not so striking or advanced that he would look
out of place on a university campus. This is Sammy Brewster.
He has fading bruises around one eye.
Sammy is polite, earnest and completely honest with the
investigators. Inviting them inside, he apologizes but says his
father is unavailable. He then makes a rather poor attempt at
preparing and serving tea in the front room. The inside of the
house is surprisingly clean, though more than one corner and
nook lies abandoned to the rot and dust. The house was designed
to be occupied by a large family, as well as two full-time staff
members, who would live in the rather spacious basement.
However, these days it is only Sammy and his father Jeremiah.
Jeremiah Brewster spends his days at The Esoteric Order
of Dagon (page 24), where he is an odd mix of a religious leader
and mafia boss, keeping the residents of the town firmly under
control so as not to upset the Deep Ones. Jeremiah is aware of
Mother Hydra’s order to sacrifice his daughter and has spent
considerable time and energy trying to convince her to come
home, where he could at least have made the death quick and
painless. However, when the time comes, he leads the chant
that reverberates through town as the people of Innsmouth give
praise to the fragment of the god emperor Cthulhu that graces
them with its presence.
However, Sammy is unaware of all of this. To him, his sister is
back in town and he’s hoping to catch up with her. He was only
eleven when she left, and his father never saw fit to share that
Ginny stole from the family. He headed up to the train, but was
intercepted by the Crew, who ran him off. He’s tried leaving her
multiple notes, but she doesn’t seem to have gotten them. His
priority is simply seeing her again.
Investigators interviewing Sammy find a friendly, honest, and
earnest young man. His father’s position has shielded him from
the uglier aspects of the town’s history, and he seems at peace
with, and genuinely looking forward to, his future below the sea.
Why wouldn’t he be? His life in town has always been wonderful
and his recent interactions with regular humans have been
rather unpleasant, further cementing his own loyalties.
Keeper note: in most cases, the investigators will recover
the Atlantean Jewel knowing that it is Ginny that stole
it; however, it might be that they recover it but still don’t
know if it was Sammy or Ginny that stole the Jewel. In this
case, the investigation may continue with the Stumbling
onto Set scene. However, once the culprit is identified, The
Epic Finale scene should begin.

In reality, Bazzledon had in fact left the Jewel with McGuire.
Ginny then stole it from the lab and took it to her old room in
The Brewster Residence (page 20) because she didn’t want
to wear it.
Investigators may have other questions, and the Keeper
should reference the Dramatis Personae for a more complete
breakdown of each NPC, and how they might answer different
questions. It is important to note that both Bazzledon and Ginny
lie frequently and easily.
If they have recovered the Jewel, the investigators can brandish
it aloft and receive huge amounts of praise from Bazzledon who
promises them a ‘great’ reward for the successful recovery,
attempting to take the Jewel from them. If the investigators hold
on to it, this provokes a stand off with the Crew. Investigators
may flee into the tunnels, or hand it over. If the investigators
return the Jewel here, then Bazzledon is wearing it during The
Epic Finale.
If the investigators accuse Ginny of the theft, she makes a large
scene, screaming at them, provoking a stand-off with the Crew,
who eventually lead the investigators off, either voluntarily, or
aggressively. If the investigators instead accuse Sammy of the
theft, everyone agrees it must have been the ‘Innsmouth boy’
and thanks the investigators for recovering it.
Eventually, McGuire gets the film going again and the NPCs
are no longer free to talk to the investigators. While they can
continue to watch filming, nothing of interest happens.
STUMBLING ONTO SET
Bright lights pain the eyes of the investigators as they round the
corner into a scene of chaos.
In front of them, Bazzledon is shouting orders, McGuire is
turning the camera arm, recording film. Behind a set of wooden
sticks that might pass for jail-cell bars in bad light, Ginny is
being dramatic, while a set of frog-like creatures poke and prod
at her with primitive looking spears. The scene is disorienting
for the investigators, whose eyes need a moment to adjust to the
bright lights.
Bazzledon is desperately trying to get Ginny to look towards
the camera and act frightened. Ginny instead wants to turn away
and sashay her hips back and forth suggestively for the camera.
Various compromises are tried before there is a sudden popping
sound from the camera and film starts flying into the air, while
McGuire grabs at it.
The tension in the room deflates. Bazzledon collapses into a
director’s chair, Ginny stamps off to a quiet corner and the Crew
deftly remove their frog suits and sit down to play some dice.
This is not the first time the camera has broken and everyone
knows they are in for a long wait while McGuire works to fix it.
The investigators now have some time where they can
interview the different NPCs, ask them questions and attempt
to get useful information from them. If the investigators are
still trying to figure out who stole the Jewel and why, they can
question the various suspects, trying to establish where they
were when the Jewel was stolen.
•
Bazzledon claims the Jewel was normally in his office,
but he left it with McGuire for ‘safekeeping’ while he
went to the grocery store. In reality, he was down in
Innsmouth speaking to members at the Esoteric Order
of Dagon.
•
Ginny claims the Jewel was always stored in Bazzledon’s
office and she hasn’t seen it. In reality, she stole it from
McGuire’s lab by sneaking through the wall.
•
McGuire doesn’t remember Bazzledon coming to see
him that day, but honestly, couldn’t say for certain. He
also didn’t hear anything unusual that night. This is
because he doesn’t pay attention.
Keeper note: if the investigators have only recently left
the Production Train, it may feel too early for them to
Stumble onto Set. Instead, have the investigators emerge
Into Innsmouth first and come back to this scene.

The General Store
The General Store is a well-known chain and laid out precisely
the same as the equivalent shop in Arkham. Though this shop is
not quite as well stocked. The store brings back into focus how
thoroughly odd Innsmouth feels, giving the investigators a taste
of mundanity throughout all the chaos.
A single employee, a young man from Arkham named
Pete, sits behind the counter. He is cheery and friendly to the
investigators. He clearly doesn’t get much business and is glad
to see some new faces.
Pete is happy to gossip about Innsmouth and how weird it
is. However, he doesn’t actually know much about the town,
commuting to work from nearby Newburyport. Pete sees
Innsmouth as simply a backwater town, dying because it can’t,
or won’t, adapt to modern times. While the fishing is good, the
little Innsmouth boats can’t compete with the modern trawlers
in the bigger ports. He says there was also some kind of disease
or epidemic a generation ago, and he thinks that’s why so many
people here look ‘kind of weird’. But you know, he’s paid hourly,
and it’s an easy job and no one bothers him or tries to convert
him to the local religion.
•
Pete doesn’t know anyone called Sammy or Ginny. He
confesses he barely knows anyone in town.
•
If the investigators are looking to get hold of some
alcohol, Pete smiles and politely directs them to a nearby
hovel, where some passable whisky can be bought from
an old lady with a fishy countenance. She is covered in
blankets.
•
Asked about Innsmouth more generally, Pete says that
he thinks the locals worship some kind of fish-god. It’s
a bit like Christianity, headquartered at the old Masonic
Lodge. He thinks the idea is that the locals worship
something that actually benefits them, like a god who
sends them more fish. He’s not one to judge.
•
If the investigators want to know more about Innsmouth,
Pete reckons their best bet is to talk to old Zadok
Allen. Zadok is a drunken old man, but is one of the few
residents of Innsmouth who seems social and interested
in talking. He pops in most mornings and talks Pete’s
ear off for half an hour before normally wandering off
looking to earn enough to buy a bottle of whiskey. On
most days, Zadok can be found  at The Fire Station
(page 23), where he either sunbathes or shelters from
the weather.
Inevitably, at some point, investigators will start asking questions
around Innsmouth. They may simply begin asking after Sammy,
or they may wish to see if they can definitively connect Ginny
to Innsmouth. Investigators may instead begin looking to see if
they can uncover any cults or otherwise malevolent forces in the
town who may be interested in stealing the Jewel.
Innsmouth is an unfriendly town. Locals avoid going out
into the street if they see the investigators passing, and many
of the roads they walk through feel completely abandoned.
Investigators can’t help but feel like they are being watched
as they move through town and may occasionally spot queer
glowing eyes following them from darkened windows.
Whatever their approach, the Keeper can suggest The
General Store (adjacent) opposite The Gilman House
Hotel (page 12) as a first port of call.
Pete

The Fire Station
Sitting on 100 Paine Street, not too far from the railway, the fire
station isn’t immediately accessible to the investigators as they
encounter a dangerous looking bridge made of rotting wood that
doesn’t seem safe to cross. While it feels fine if the investigators
cross it one at a time, anyone with a SIZ greater than 70 must pass
a Luck roll or the rotten wood snaps, dropping the investigator
into the Manuxet river, taking 1D6 damage and washing up three
blocks down. The bridge certainly couldn’t hold the weight of a
car, or the one operational fire engine, putting large portions of
town at risk if the fire department was ever required (not that
the damp, rotten wood of Innsmouth would necessarily burn all
that well.)
Investigators looking for Zadok Allen find him here, resting
himself against the stone outer wall of the fire station. It looks as
if no one is manning the station today and he is all alone.
Zadok is grumpy, difficult, and uninterested in talking to a
group of strangers at first. They need to loosen his lips with a
bottle of whisky. However, if the investigators do tempt him with
a tipple, he leads them away from the station, to a nice sheltered
house on the edge of town looking out towards the cliff face.
Zadok Allen is the infamous drunk from The Shadow over
Innsmouth, and knows the full story of Obed Marsh, his deal
with the Deep Ones and the three oaths the people of Innsmouth
were forced to swear. He shares a fragmented, confused story of
what happened with the investigators, similar to what a Call of
Cthulhu Keeper may share if they were trying to recite the story
of The Shadow over Innsmouth from memory.
•
When sharing the story of Innsmouth with the
investigators, Zadok focuses on the fact that the Deep
Ones punish those they feel have broken the oaths. And
rumors abound that ‘something big’ is going to happen
to an oath breaker tonight.
•
If asked about Sammy or Ginny, he replies “Jeremiah’s
kids? Sammy & Ginny Brewster, right? Good kids. Good
family.’ He mentions a townhouse just off Lafayette
street, The Brewster Residence.
•
If the investigators describe the Atlantean Jewel to him,
he shushes them and ells them not to talk about the holy
symbols of the Esoteric Order of Dagon in public. ‘They’
could be listening.
Eventually, Zadok grows too jumpy, staring out at the sea, and
when the Keeper feels the time is right, Zadok screams, “They’ve
heard us,” and bolts away from the investigators. If they follow
him, they eventually find him hiding inside a ruined house not
far from the Fire Station, crying and completely unresponsive.
Zadok Allen
Jeremiah Brewster

Entering through the Caves
The underground entrance to the Esoteric Order of Dagon
through the Cave System is not guarded. It is mostly used as a
way for Deep Ones to quickly enter and leave the temple without
having to walk out in the open, and the Deep Ones see no need
to guard their pathways.
As the investigators step out into the basement level, the small
stone room is empty, apart from a number of storage boxes.
The rotten smell of fish and seaweed is almost enough to make
someone gag. Investigators hear a croaking kind of song coming
through the doorway. On a successful Listen roll they hear the
words: “Cthulhu fhtagn!” repeated over and over.
Investigators peeking out from the doorway see a large room
of worship, similar to many churches they have seen. At the
front of the room stand three statues. The largest in the center
is of Cthulhu, a maddening head of tentacles, piercing eyes and
unfathomably large wings that seem to spread out to engulf
the entire building. Two smaller statues of Dagon and Mother
Hydra flank the main statue (fish-like quadrupedal creatures
with terrifying teeth. One looks built like a fighter, the other has
wide-hips, a motherly figure).
A fish-like man (Jeremiah Brewster) seems to be praying and
singing the song they hear. On his head sits a tiara of gold alloy
that looks identical to the Jewel.
Patient investigators may sit and watch. After five minutes,
Jeremiah finishes his chanting and walks towards the room
where the investigators are. They could easily ambush him at
this moment, or while he is singing. However, Jeremiah is a
powerful Sorcerer and any loud actions draw the attention of
dozens of Hybrids.
If the investigators are overwhelmed in the fight, they need
not die. They can be knocked out and wake up tied up for the
Epic Finale (page 25) atop the cliff face, for the Playing the
Hero (page 27) outcome.
The Esoteric Order of Dagon
Speaking to Sammy or Zadok may lead the investigators to
believe that the Jewel is connected to the Esoteric Order of
Dagon. This is wrong; however if investigators get hooked into
this pattern, the Keeper can encourage it, having them visit the
Esoteric Order of Dagon.
Sitting prominently on Federal Street in the center of town,
this neo-classical building is hard to miss. Four Grecian
columns frame the main doorway, though the whitewash has
faded to a dull gray. Above the door, a large stone carving of the
words ‘Esoteric Order of Dagon’ stands prominently across the
building. This building is a converted Masonic temple and is by
far the grandest building in Innsmouth.
Four heavy-looking Hybrids lounge around the entranceway
and they will stop the investigators if they try and approach
the door directly. The Hybrids have a strong ‘Innsmouth Look’
about them and are quick to use a slap or gut punch to move
on any investigators that seem overly inquisitive about temple
matters.
Investigators circling the building realize that there are no
windows or other doorways other than the front entrance.
However, with a successful Natural World roll, they notice
that behind the temple, the way the rocks fall indicate there
might be a way in through the Caves. Investigators deciding to
keep watch on the building for a while must pass a Stealth roll
to not get moved on by the watchful Hybrids. If they do manage
to watch the building, they notice the same person leaving the
building twice in a row about an hour apart. There must be
another way inside.
If investigators are unable to enter the building and wish to,
the Keeper may consider a Know roll to lead the investigators
into the Cave System, looking for another way inside.

The promised storm finally washes over Innsmouth and rain
begins pouring down over the half-rotten buildings. What little
sun remains is covered by thick black clouds and the world
noticeably darkens around the investigators. Looking up to the
cliffs above Innsmouth, the investigators see a camera, pointing
at a woman dressed all in white. Ginny Dubois looks as if she
has been tied to a large stone on the very edge of the cliff, her
hands bound above her so that her white body makes a striking
X-shape against the darkened stone.
In sleepy Innsmouth, the residents pour out onto the streets.
Where just a few moments ago, they were abandoned, now
they are thronged with people, all staring up towards the
cliff face. Regular humans stand shoulder-to-shoulder with
twisted hybrids and fully transformed Deep Ones. Meanwhile,
in the shallow bay, the waves are roiling and investigators see
hundreds of yellow eyes peering out from just under the water.
Every single person’s gaze is fixed upon that white X above the
cliffs. This all prompts a Sanity roll (1/1D8). Investigators
going insane here may choose to roll on the regular bout of
insanity table or instead choose to be caught up in the moment
and follow along with the crowd as they stare and chant.
A slow chant begins. It can first be heard from those nearest
to the Esoteric Order of Dagon. Before slowly rolling out across
all of Innsmouth.
“Ph’nglui mglw’nafh Cthulhu R’lyeh wgah’nagl fhtagn Iä! Iä!
Cthulhu fhtagn”
If the investigators continue to watch, the roiling clouds
become thicker and thicker out over the shallow reef just outside
Innsmouth Harbour. And somehow, in a trick of the light, the
clouds are suddenly a mass of tentacles with a set of piercing
eyes at its center. A Star-Spawn of Cthulhu hangs over the bay.
Every single resident in Innsmouth drops to their knees in silent
prayer to this shard of a god.
The Star-Spawn’s visage is hidden behind the clouds, and the
investigators may have already decided to run, so they likely do
not fully comprehend the thing in the clouds However, if they
persist on peering past the clouds (and are not already insane)
then viewing the Star-Spawn directly prompts a Sanity roll
(1D6/1D20).
At this point, investigators may go off in many different
directions. Some possible resolutions to the story are below, but
if the investigators choose a different path then events continue
to unfold around them no matter what.
The Last Train out of Innsmouth
Investigators choosing to take flight, either through the crowds,
or the caves below have the gaze of the Star Spawn fall on them,
and it attempts to apprehend them, sending the citizenry and its
pseudopodia to capture them
If they flee through the crowds, hands grab at them from
all directions and the press of people quickly pins them down,
suffocating them. They are tied up and offered up to the Star
Spawn as further sacrifices. Move to Playing the Hero (page
27).
If the investigators take to the caves, they are instead pursued
by mindless, tentacled creatures that crawl rapidly through the
caves. The investigators spend three rounds being pursued. If
they fail to pass a DEX roll, then 1D3 tentacles attack them
(Brawl 50%, 1D3 damage). Investigators can also argue for
different rolls as they rush through the dark, dangerous caves.
Erupting out onto the edge of town, the investigators see Anna
Díaz and three surviving members of the Crew busily packing up
their belongings and loading it up on the train.  The wind is now
blowing a gale, and they all determinedly avoid looking southeast towards the Star Spawn. Díaz screams into the wind as they
approach, asking if any of them know how to drive a train.
The firebox of the train has been kept alight, and until recently
a member of the crew was cooking eggs on the hot metal.
Investigators passing an Operate Heavy Machinery or
Mechanical Repair roll know that they need to repressurize
the boiler by turning the cylinder cocks, and gently opening the
regulator. This requires that the investigators pass three STR
rolls and three DEX rolls within three rounds. At the end of the
third round, a mob of Innsmouth residents descend on the train
car, quickly overwhelming everyone.
If the investigators do get the train up and running, it lets
out a piercing whistle, building momentum slowly as it begins
running down the ancient track. The last train out of Innsmouth
rolls away, taking the surviving investigators and crew with
them.
Alternatively the train could be sabotaged to try and stop the
advancing horrors, or driven directly into the approaching mob
(see box, page 26).
Once the investigation nears completion, and the investigators
have a clear understanding that Ginny Dubois is the culprit, then
the Epic Finale begins. This could happen anywhere around
Innsmouth, though it is best for the moment to happen whilst
the investigators are in town.
Keeper note: have the investigators failed to identify
Ginny as the culprit and failed to pick up on all your
wonderful clues? Or have they instead pissed off the locals
and been captured? Don’t worry, just start the Epic Finale
anyway.

MVR Class B1 ‘Olmstead’, steam locomotive
MOV: 11
Build: 10
Armour for people: 1
Gauge: standard (4 ft 8 1⁄2 in)
Boiler pressure: 110 psi
Top Speed: 70 mph (110 km/h)
Driving the train requires a successful Drive Train or Operate Heavy Machinery roll. If the build is reduced to
zero, the train is out of action. Each full 10 hit points of damage decreases a train’s build by 1 point (round down);
damage below 10 hit points is ignored.
If the train’s build is reduced to half (round down) of its starting value or lower, it is impaired; one penalty die is
applied to all Drive Train (or appropriate skill) rolls.
If a train takes damage equal to its full build value in one incident, the vehicle is completely wrecked in an
impressive manner. It may explode, burn, roll or suffer some combination thereof. Anyone on the footplate of the
train, roll Luck. Success leads to enough of their remains being found to identify them. Anyone within 50m (165 ft)
of the engine takes 6D10 damage. Anyone outside of that area and not behind cover makes a Dodge roll. Failure
results in being hit with high velocity debris (2D4 damage). Alternatively, such an explosion could be caused by
dangerously increasing the pressure in the boiler, with a successful Drive Train, Operate Heavy Machinery,
or Hard Science (Physics) roll.
If a train’s build is otherwise reduced to zero by cumulative damage (i.e. in increments of less than the vehicle’s
starting build value), it becomes undriveable, grinding to a halt. Depending on the situation (and perhaps a Luck
roll), this may lead to an accident resulting in 1D10 damage for the driver and each passenger.

Allow the investigator a Hard DEX or Throw roll to determine
if they manage to drop the Tum-Eez into the creature’s mouth
before they are torn to shreds and eaten by the Star-Spawn.
If they fail, then Bazzledon turns to the next investigator and
repeats the lines verbatim:
“You’ve always wanted to be on the silver screen haven’t you.
I know you have, kid…”
If the investigators succeed, they are, unfortunately, still
torn to shreds by the monster. It turns out that antacids have
no effect on the Star-Spawn. However, in achieving the final
shot, the movie is completed, and Bazzledon turns around, cuts
McGuire’s throat, and lopes off into the wilderness with the film
under his arm.
Investigators who overcome Bazzledon’s charms see him for
what he truly is, a madman, sending innocents to die. As they
turn to flee, there is a sudden calm in the storm and the chanting
ceases. With a cry of despair, Ginny Brewster is torn to shreds in
front of the silent denizens of Innsmouth. Her body is dropped
carelessly down into the ocean, not even given the honor of being
food for the god shard. This prompts a Sanity roll (1/1D6).
Investigators may flee over the open ground away from
Innsmouth, or come down to the train to find everyone dead,
torn to shreds as they made a valiant attempt to escape from
the monster on the train. By one way or another, the surviving
investigators return to Arkham.
Playing the Hero
Investigators making their way determinedly up to the cliffs to
the sacrifice experience no violent retribution from the Star-
Spawn. In fact, the road clears ahead of them, as they rush up
the winding path towards the climatic moment. The same events
unfold if they are captured and brought up against their will.
As they approach, they see Christopher McGuire slowly
turning the handle of the camera. His eyes are glazed and he
is completely unresponsive. Ginny has been torn from the rock
where she was tied, leaving behind a pentagram, clearly drawn
in blood smeared across it. She is now in the clutches of the
tentacles above, screaming for help. A number of Crew members
lie in pieces around the site, their bodies seemingly torn to
shreds by tentacles whilst attempting to save her.
Bazzledon is on his knees, screaming along to the chant
from the town below. When the investigators arrive, his eyes
snap open and he turns to them, rushing over to whichever
investigator seems to most closely fit with the stereotype of
the hero who saves the day. Failing that, he moves towards the
investigator with the highest APP and casts the spell Mental
Suggestion (page 30).
“You’ve always wanted to be on the silver screen haven’t you.
I know you have, kid. This is your big moment, your time to
shine. You’re gonna be a movie star. Take this,…” He hands
the investigator a packet of Tum-Eez antacid “… run up that
tentacle, and drop it in the things mouth. It’ll overwhelm it,
sending it back to its watery grave.”
The investigator needs to pass a POW roll to resist the urge
to do exactly what Bazzledon suggests. Though their fellow
investigators may also attempt to stop them, by grappling with
them. If the investigator fails the roll, they run towards the Star-
Spawn, attempting to climb up one of the tentacles towards the
creature’s terrifying mouth.
What if they’re captured?
Captured investigators wake up tied-up on the cliff-face
and see the Epic Finale playing out in front of them. The
Star Spawn appears, Ginny tied to the rock. But instead
of trudging up and being approached by Bazzledon, their
bindings are cut loose by Bazzledon as he gives his pep talk
and hands them the Tum-Eez.

hit new film taking the underworld by storm. The graphics are
so realistic, you’d swear the dame was actually torn apart. And
it’s in technicolor! The marvels of the modern age…

Did the investigators escape with the Atlantean Jewel?
If they did, Miskatonic University is incredibly pleased with
the Society. They agree to the next 12 months funding up front.
Further, the Society is offered a much nicer room for future
meetings. One with a fireplace and far comfier seats usually
reserved for faculty.
If they did not, it is the beginning of the end for the Society.
Another important mission fumbled, the University begins
reconsidering its long-standing support. Perhaps it is time
they brought some experts in, rather than trusting a group of
amateurs.
A few weeks after the end of the investigation, an internal
review docks Dr. Henry Armitage one week’s wages for ‘failing
to properly check the credentials of an applicant’ and the matter
